title: promote-latest step 1 accepts a failed Release run only under DEC-204 (a4)'s Windows-probe excuse
description: opum-doc ruling DEC-204 (a4), 2026-10-20T09:05Z, relayed by team-lead under DEC-182. scripts/promote-latest.mjs step 1 (checkReleaseRun) refuses any Release run that did not conclude success, so run 39366418979 (v0.14.1 dry run, the run the pair receipt names and whose artifact was staged) can never be promoted: its two Windows release-gate-probe arms fail at setup-quest, which refuses a source build on Windows while quest 0.14.1 is not on npm (ETARGET), and the probe never runs there. Change: a run that concluded failure is accepted ONLY when ALL FOUR hold: (1) every failed job is a Windows release-gate-probe arm; (2) each such arm log shows the setup-quest Windows refusal and no other ##[error] line; (3) @opum-ai/quest@<version> was not installable from npm at the run start, measured from npm own time[<version>] against the run created_at, never against now, an absent publish time counting as not installable; (4) every other job concluded success. Anything else refuses as today and the refusal names the failed condition. When it applies one line names the excused jobs and DEC-204 (a4). Proof through the injectable runner with no network: accepted on 39366418979 shape; refused by name for a non-Windows failure, a Windows probe failing another way, a Windows probe with an extra ##[error], and quest already installable at run start; a mutation disabling the check reddens the refusal tests, its prediction committed first. Scoped to promote-latest.mjs; the same excuse lands in publish-release.sh under LCLI-742 for the next pair, and the real fix (setup-quest on Windows) belongs in the next pair plan and retires this excuse.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED, opum-ai/lore-cli#625, head 62ba21d1f414f999332065503ec2633d289c72f0

I'm a read-only DEC-183 reviewer on opus-5-5. I read the diff and the files at the head SHA. I ran nothing.

ITEMS
1. Conditions implemented as ruled: REFUTED. Two places are wider than the ruling. Everything else matches.
   - Error-line order and count: CONFIRMED. scripts/promote-latest.mjs:811-829.
     - Refusal anywhere: `!annotations.some(isRefusal)` refuses.
     - Refusal not first: `!isRefusal(annotations[0])` refuses.
     - Anything after the first line that is not the generic exit line: the `strangers` check refuses.
     - More than two lines: `annotations.length > 2` refuses.
     - So the only accepted sets are [refusal] and [refusal, generic]. A second refusal line counts as a stranger and refuses.
     - errorAnnotations (:726-731) counts only lines that start with `##[error]` after the timestamp is stripped. An `echo` in the step's source does not count.
     - MINOR: isRefusal is a prefix match (:812, :716). It is not an exact match on the full line that action.yml:117 emits, and that line is deterministic once RUNNER_OS=Windows is filled in.
   - Reads only time["<version>"]: CONFIRMED. :846 reads only `times[version]` from `npm view @opum-ai/quest time` (:291-293). It refuses at `publishedAt <= startedAt` against created_at (:853).
     - Unreadable, non-object or unparseable values refuse (:837-852). A missing or unparseable created_at refuses (:833-835).
     - MINOR: :847 checks the VALUE (`!== undefined && !== null`), not the KEY. A key that is present but null is therefore read as absent, and a present non-string is passed to Date.parse. Use `Object.hasOwn(times, version)` and refuse any present value that is not a string. Real npm output never produces this.
   - Named-skip set: REFUTED, because it is wider than ruled. All three patterns at :709-714 are anchored at the start only: `/^publish \(npm, OIDC trusted publishing\)/`, `/^verify this release's own provenance/` and `/^Ladybug optional 1 GiB observation/`.
     - Any skipped job whose name merely starts with one of these is excused, so a lookalike CAN slip in.
     - The publish guard has the same weakness: :778 uses `jobs.find` and reads only the first job that matches PUBLISH_JOB.
     - Nothing collides at this tag. The names come from release.yml at the tagged commit (:485, :1152, :1737), and those are reviewed code. This is still the lookalike case the brief asked me to rule out.
     - Fix: match the three full names in release.yml exactly (Ladybug needs its "(ubuntu-24.04 x64)" suffix), and refuse unless exactly one job is the publish job.
   - Publish present and skipped: CONFIRMED, apart from the first-match issue above. When the publish job is absent or not skipped, :779-782 adds a refusal for the whole run. An absent publish job is stricter than the ruling requires, not wider.
     - Note: publish `needs: release-gate-probe` (release.yml:1161), so publish is skipped whenever a probe fails, even on a publish:true run. "Publish skipped" therefore still proves nothing was published, which is exactly what ruling D relies on.
   - Condition 1: CONFIRMED. A Windows arm counts only when conclusion === "failure" (:789-791). cancelled, timed_out, null and neutral all count as "others" and refuse (:792-796). A run with no failed job refuses (:797-800).
2. Fail-closed: REFUTED, by one path.
   - BLOCKING: :768 is `Number.isInteger(jobsDoc.total_count) && total_count > jobs.length`. If `total_count` is absent or not an integer, the check is skipped and a partial list is accepted.
     - Fix: refuse unless `Number.isInteger(total_count) && total_count === jobs.length`.
     - Add a test with total_count deleted. The existing "cut off" case covers only a value that is present but too large.
   - CONFIRMED by reading:
     - Jobs unreadable: the throw is caught and refused (:761-766).
     - No job list: refused (:767-773).
     - More than one page: per_page=100 (:282), and total_count > length refuses. A run with 101+ jobs cannot pass.
     - Log unreadable: caught at :805-809, and that condition 2 entry is then refused at :861.
     - Empty log: zero annotations, which takes the "does not show refusal" branch and refuses.
     - npm time unreadable: refused.
     - Cancelled arm: refused.
     - Failure with no failed job: refused.
   - UNTESTED: a missing (404) arm log and an empty arm log have no refusal case. Each is a one-line case in the existing harness: leave one arm's id out of jobLogs, or set its log to "".
3. Happy path and the rest of the file unchanged: CONFIRMED. The .mjs has five hunks:
   - header comment, :33-37
   - three argv builders, :276-293
   - the `excused` parameter, which defaults to false and waives ONLY the conclusion line, :676-690
   - the new block, :702-863
   - main step 1, :1538-1565
   - The excuse is evaluated only when conclusion === "failure" AND checkReleaseRun with the conclusion waived finds nothing else wrong (:1541-1543).
     - A successful run never reads its jobs. Test :677 asserts zero job reads and no DEC-204 output.
     - A failed run of another commit refuses on head_sha and reads no jobs. Test :663 covers this.
   - checkReleaseRun has no other callers, and the existing LCLI-621 tests at :2132-2155 are unchanged.
   - Nothing after :1565 changed.
4. Tests are real: REFUTED on fixture fidelity.
   - The accepted fixture (test :384-396) has 8 jobs: 4 successes, 2 named skips (Ladybug, publish) and 2 Windows failures.
   - It has no "verify this release's own provenance (LCLI-481)" job. That job skips on every publish:false run (release.yml:1754), so the real run has 3 named skips and about 20 successes, not 2 and 4.
   - As a result, the second SKIPPED_BY_CONSTRUCTION pattern is never exercised. Deleting it or misspelling it leaves all 243 tests green, while the real dry run on 39366418979 would refuse.
   - The brief's block list does not cover this, because it fails closed. I'm asking for it anyway since changes are already requested. Either of these closes it:
     - (a) rebuild the accepted fixture from the real 25-job dump of 39366418979, or
     - (b) attach the real `--dry-run` output against 39366418979 before landing. That is LCLI-744 AC5, still unchecked; it moves nothing.
   - What does hold:
     - refusalSuite (test :854-873) asserts exit 1, the condition-specific message and expectRefusedBeforeAnyWrite, in both modes. Removing a check therefore turns its case red by message even when some other condition still refuses.
     - The mutations target what they claim:
       - M2: `publishedAt <= startedAt`
       - M3: strangers
       - M4: `> 2`
       - M5: annotations[0]
       - M6: the publish guard
       - M7: the `.some`
       - M1: the final `return refuse()`. The jobs-unreadable and jobs-cut-off cases return earlier, which is why they stay green under M1.
   - MINOR: the test named "platform key" (:513) uses "0.13.0", which is another version, not a platform key. The code reads only the root package's time map, so this is harmless.
5. Runbook: CONFIRMED with nits. docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:1135-1148 states all four conditions, the named skips, the publish-present-and-skipped rule and "setup-quest on Windows retires this exception".
   - Nit: it says "no npm publish time BEFORE created_at", but the code also refuses when the times are equal (`<=`).
   - Nit: numbered item 1 (:1153-1155) still says "a successful run" and does not point to the exception.
   - It does not name the next pair's plan or ruling E. Those live in LCLI-742's notes.
6. No change to publishing, dist-tags, auth or the receipt gate: CONFIRMED. Nothing after step 1 changed. The only new outbound calls are three reads: gh jobs, gh job log, and anonymous `npm view time` with ANONYMOUS pins.

FINDINGS, ranked
1. BLOCKING: a missing total_count fails open (:768).
2. BLOCKING, because it widens the ruling: the named-skip and publish regexes are prefix-only, and the publish guard reads only the first match (:709-714, :778).
3. SHOULD-FIX: the accepted fixture is not 39366418979's shape, and the provenance named skip is never tested. Close it with (a) or (b) under item 4.
4. MINOR: no tests for a 404 or empty arm log.
5. MINOR: absent time is decided by value rather than key (:847).
6. MINOR: isRefusal is a prefix match, not an exact match (:812).
7. NIT: the runbook's "before" vs the code's `<=`, and item 1 has no cross-reference to the exception.

COULD NOT CHECK WITHOUT A SHELL
- The real jobs list and logs of 39366418979: the job count, exact names, the timestamp and BOM shape, and whether the composite action emits exactly one generic exit line.
- Whether `gh api .../actions/jobs/<id>/logs` follows its 302 redirect. If it does not, stdout is empty and the run refuses, which fails closed.
- The shape of npm 12's output for `npm view @opum-ai/quest time --json`.
- That the 243/0 result and the mutation results reproduce.
- Full `bun test` and `bun run lore check`. test/ pins runbook text, so the docs edit needs both.
- The PR's CI run on 62ba21d1.
=== END ===
